claims.statement: main() is a thin wrapper that awaits run() and reports a fatal error through crash::report_startup_failure; run() owns OS-facing startup: CLI parsing, data directory, single-instance claim, panic hook, logging with defaults, bootstrap(), logging with the configured settings, autostart, optional Aria2 RPC, then UI construction.

build_ui is deliberately synchronous and timer-free, taking pre-resolved UiBootInputs; it builds the real MainWindow, applies translation and appearance, arms sleep inhibition from the loaded settings, constructs AppContext and registers all handlers, which is the seam that makes headless UI tests possible.

AppContext holds the window/weak handle, Dispatcher, EventBus, task store, toast queue, RPC shutdown sender, new-task torrent scratch state, inspector/Labs state and tray flag; settings() reads through the dispatcher and is explicitly not a cache.
src/bridge is a pure mapping layer re-exporting models, forms (split by settings section), task_store, format, clipboard, labs, piece_map and setup_wizard modules with no window dependency.
List-style editors (schedule slots, disk-type overrides, Aria2 clients) keep their editing state in the UI model and are parsed by Rust only at Save; the Aria2 client editor persists only token_hash.

handlers::register_all wires one register() per subsystem (task, new_task, inspector, settings, setup_wizard, labs, updater, window), and handlers/common.rs owns the binding boilerplate such as with_ui, read_ui, mutate_store, reload_tasks and TaskAction.

The desktop EventBus subscriber matches every DownloadEvent variant explicitly, ignores Aria2Notification, and recovers from RecvError::Lagged by replacing the whole store from Dispatcher::list() because partial replay is impossible.
on_updated detects removal by asking Dispatcher::status for the task and dropping the row and closing the inspector when the backend no longer knows the task.

push_toast appends to a shared queue and spawns a task that, after the requested duration, marks the entry leaving and drops it after TOAST_EXIT_MS; dismiss_toast uses the same retire path, and WarningDedup collapses the same id:message warning within a 5-second window because core emits one warning per peer/mirror/disk check.

settings_sync::SettingsSync centralizes post-save side effects shared by the settings dialog and setup wizard — autostart sync, Aria2 RPC hot reload, and push_ui for language/tray/appearance/default directory plus the power.prevent_sleep re-application — and push_ui disarms reset_confirm on every close path.

Rust-side dynamic text must go through i18n::format_* helpers (split by domain) rather than hardcoded CJK, .slint text uses @tr, and a test fails when a @tr string is missing from any of the three PO catalogs.

Single-instance claiming uses a session-local named mutex with FindWindowW/WM_COPYDATA activation on Windows and an exclusive advisory lock on <data-dir>/instance.lock with a Unix domain socket activation channel elsewhere; notify_primary returns whether the request reached a primary and the socket path falls back to a hashed temp name past the sun_path budget.

Every autostart registration appends --hidden; Windows uses HKCU Run (or the MSIX startupTask extension), Linux an XDG .desktop, and macOS a LaunchAgent, and a moved executable triggers re-registration.

Window geometry restoration uses GetWindowPlacement/SetWindowPos and monitor checks on Windows but Slint's size/position plus a MAX_PLAUSIBLE_COORD (±20000 px) heuristic in platform_win.rs elsewhere, and schedule_window_placement_restore retries ensure_restored_window_placement every 250 ms until the OS window exists.

ui/theme.slint (generated from xtask/src/theme.rs) exposes a Theme global whose mode comes from appearance.color_mode and accent from appearance.theme_color via the ColorModePref and ThemeAccent (Lime/Amber/Sky/Violet/Monochrome) enums; apply_appearance translates settings into that global plus the OS window theme.

The shared autostart `expected_command` helper (quoted exe path plus --hidden) is compiled only on Windows and Linux; macOS builds its LaunchAgent plist ProgramArguments array from `current_exe_string` directly.
A fatal startup error is surfaced twice: written to the crash log and shown in a localized rfd message box whose language comes from the OS locale, because settings may not have loaded.

The panic hook writes timestamp, thread, file:line, payload and a captured backtrace to <state_dir>/logs/crash.log and echoes it to stderr, rotating to crash.log.1 past 1 MiB; it runs even under panic = "abort", which makes any catch_unwind a development-only safety net.

Building the tray icon is best-effort: a missing StatusNotifier host logs tray_init_failure_message and startup continues, because the window is the primary UI and aborting there would take the window down with it.

On Unix a SIGTERM/SIGINT watcher asks the Slint event loop to quit, so logout, systemctl stop and Ctrl+C run the normal graceful shutdown (buffer flush, manifest persist, WAL checkpoint) instead of killing the process mid-write; Windows has no console to catch.

sync_toasts reconciles the live Slint toasts model in place through apply_toasts, updating rows whose id survives and inserting only new ids, so dismissing one toast does not recreate and re-animate the others.

The toast card in ui/components/toast_stack.slint slides in from the right on creation and slides back out when the toast's leaving flag flips, driven by an entered flag that a one-shot Timer sets; Rust keeps the entry for TOAST_EXIT_MS (240 ms), longer than the 200 ms animation.

summary_to_task_item derives TaskItem::is_indeterminate (Queued with zero downloaded bytes, or Downloading with zero downloaded bytes and an unknown or zero total); task_card.slint and task_table.slint render indeterminate rows with a 1500 ms flowing highlight beam and animate the determinate bar width over 250 ms, and the update-download and CDN-speedtest bars reuse that width animation.

The desktop task list is reconciled in place: apply_tasks set_row_data-mutates the existing VecModel<TaskItem> model with a same-order fast path and a remove/align general path instead of replacing it, so Slint row components keep hover/double-click state and an open context menu is not dismissed by progress events.

The tray menu is built with muda and refreshed on the UI thread by update_tray_menu_and_tooltip, and on Linux it is a D-Bus StatusNotifierItem whose icon build is best-effort so a missing host degrades to window-only operation instead of failing the launch.

power.rs keeps one process-wide PowerGuard whose desired state is `enabled && active downloads > 0`, latched behind a single mutex so that only a change of desire reaches the OS API — a rejected acquire is therefore logged once per rising edge instead of retried on every UI refresh, and racing callers cannot take two locks or release each other's.

Each desktop platform has its own RAII keep-awake backend: Windows SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS|ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED|ES_AWAYMODE_REQUIRED) with the acquiring thread recorded (the flag is thread-local), macOS an IOKit PreventUserIdleSystemSleep power assertion, and Linux logind Inhibit("idle:sleep", ..., "block") whose returned pipe fd is the lock; other targets keep a no-op guard.

The keep-awake lock is driven by two inputs only — the download count reported by refresh_ui/event_stream::bus and power.prevent_sleep, which is armed at boot by build_ui and re-applied by SettingsSync::push_ui on the UI thread because the Windows flag is thread-local; release() is called on the exit paths.

Sleep inhibition never overrides the lid, a shutdown request or a privileged suspend, never keeps the display on, and degrades to a logged warning without stopping the download when the platform service refuses (for example a logind polkit denial on a session that is not active).
